entities.name: Pierre de la Vergne
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pierre de la Vergne, also known by various Latinized forms such as Petrus de Vernio or the French appellations Pierre de Veruche, Pierre Verneyo, Pierre Veruco, Pierre Verrujo, and Pierre Veroche, was a prominent French cardinal whose career unfolded during the tumultuous era of the Western Schism. Elevated to the cardinalate by Antipope Clement VII in 1385, de la Vergne became a staunch adherent of the Avignon Papacy, playing a role in the ecclesiastical and political machinations that divided Latin Christendom for nearly four decades. His life, concluding with his death on October 15, 1403, exemplifies the profound challenges to papal authority and the deep factionalism that characterized the late Medieval Church, shaping the careers and loyalties of countless clergy.

Born in the Limousin region of France, likely in the diocese of Limoges, Pierre de la Vergne pursued an ecclesiastical career that saw him rise through the ranks. Before his elevation, he served as Archbishop of Auch from 1375 to 1383, and then as Archbishop of Clermont from 1383 until his cardinalate. These appointments positioned him firmly within the French ecclesiastical hierarchy that had supported the Avignon popes since the return of Gregory XI to Rome in 1377 and the subsequent election of Urban VI, which precipitated the Schism. As a cardinal, he resided in Avignon, contributing to the administrative and diplomatic efforts of Clement VII and later Benedict XIII to assert their legitimacy against the Roman pontiffs.
